en.text: The Church of Saint Sava is a Serbian Orthodox church in Belgrade, capital of Serbia. It is the fourth largest Eastern Orthodox church in the world and one of the largest churches in the world by gross volume.

places.nameLocal: Рушевине Народне библиотеке из нацистичког бомбардовања 1941.

names.en: Ruins of National Library from 1941 Nazi bombing
names.local: Рушевине Народне библиотеке из нацистичког бомбардовања 1941.

he.text: הספרייה הלאומית של סרביה היא הספרייה הלאומית של סרביה הממוקמת בבלגרד והספרייה הגדולה במדינה.

en.text: The National Library of Serbia is the national library of Serbia, located in the capital city of Belgrade. It is the largest library and oldest institution in Serbia, having been destroyed multiple times over the last two centuries.

The National Museum of Serbia is the largest and oldest museum in Belgrade, Serbia. It is located in the central zone of Belgrade on a square plot between the Republic Square, formerly Theatre Square, and three streets: Čika Ljubina, Vasina and Laze Pačua.

he.text: מצודת בלגרד היא מצודה השוכנת בתחום המוניציפלי של בלגרד בירת סרביה. המצודה הוקמה כקסטרום בראשית המאה ה-1 עת נשלט האזור על ידי הקיסרות הרומית והוקפה בחומת עץ.

en.text: The Belgrade Fortress is a cultural monument in Belgrade, Serbia in the municipality of Stari Grad. It consists of the old citadel and Kalemegdan Park on the confluence of the Sava and Danube rivers.

The Kalemegdan Park, or simply Kalemegdan is the largest park and the most important historical monument in Belgrade. It is located on a 125-metre-high cliff, at the junction of the River Sava and the Danube.

he.text: בית הפרחים הוא מאוזוליאום בעיר בלגרד שבסרביה, המשמש כמקום קבורתו של נשיא יוגוסלביה יוסיפ ברוז טיטו.

en.text: The House of Flowers is the resting place of Josip Broz Tito and Jovanka Broz, the President and the First Lady of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. It is located on the grounds of the Museum of Yugoslavia in Dedinje, Belgrade, Serbia.
The Bajrakli Mosque is a mosque in Belgrade, Serbia. Built around 1575, it is the only mosque in the city out of the 273 that had existed during the time of the Ottoman Empire's rule of Serbia.

names.ja: ニコラ・テスラ博物館

he.text: מוזיאון ניקולה טסלה הוא מוזיאון מדע הממוקם במרכז בלגרד, בירת סרביה. הוא מוקדש לכבוד ולהצגה של חייו ופועלו של ניקולה טסלה, וזהו גם מקום קבורתו.

en.text: The Nikola Tesla Museum is a science museum located in Belgrade in Serbia. It is dedicated to honoring and displaying the life and work of Nikola Tesla as well as the final resting place for Tesla.

names.ja: 強制収容所オールドフェア

he.text: סַיְימישטֶה היה מחנה ריכוז והשמדה נאצי שהיה ממוקם בפאתי בלגרד, על שטחה של מדינת קרואטיה העצמאית בתקופת מלחמת העולם השנייה. מוכר בספרות המחקרית גם כ"מחנה זֶמְלִין".

en.text: The Sajmište concentration camp was a Nazi German concentration and extermination camp during World War II. It was located at the former Belgrade fairground site near the town of Zemun, in the Independent State of Croatia.

The Church of Saint Mark is an Eastern Orthodox church located in Belgrade, Serbia. The church, dedicated to Mark the Evangelist is situated in the Tašmajdan park, near the House of the National Assembly, in the downtown Belgrade.

names.en: Cathedral Church of St. Michael the Archangel
names.ja: 聖天使首ミハイル大聖堂 (ベオグラード)

en.text: The Cathedral of Saint Archangel Michael, commonly known as the Cathedral church, is an Eastern Orthodox church located in Belgrade, Serbia. It is under jurisdiction of the Archdiocese of Belgrade and Karlovci of the Serbian Orthodox Church and serves as its cathedral church.
The Ada Bridge is a cable-stayed bridge over the Sava River in Belgrade, Serbia. The bridge crosses the tip of Ada Ciganlija island, connecting the municipalities of Čukarica and New Belgrade.
The Republic Square or the Square of the Republic is one of the central town squares and an urban neighborhood of Belgrade, located in the Stari Grad municipality.

Singidunum was an ancient city which later evolved into modern Belgrade, the capital of Serbia. The name is of Celtic origin, going back to the time when the Celtic tribe Scordisci settled the area in the 3rd century BC, following the Gallic invasion of the Balkans.

The Museum of Yugoslavia is a public history museum in Belgrade, Serbia dedicated to the history of Yugoslavia and the life of Josip Broz Tito. Tito and his wife Jovanka are buried on the museum's grounds in the House of Flowers.

names.es: Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Belgrado
names.zh-CN: 貝爾格勒當代藝術博物館
names.ja: 現代美術館 (ベオグラード)
names.de: Museum für zeitgenössische Kunst in Belgrad

en.text: The Museum of Contemporary Art is an art museum located in Belgrade, Serbia. It was founded in 1958 as the Modern Gallery, making it one of the first museums of this type in the world.

he.text: בית הכנסת סוכת שלום הוא בית כנסת שפעיל בבלגרד בירת סרביה. ב-2013 הוכרז המבנה כאתר מורשת סרבית.

en.text: The Belgrade Synagogue, officially the Sukkat Shalom Synagogue, is an Orthodox Jewish congregation and synagogue, located in downtown Belgrade, Serbia. The only functioning synagogue in the country, the Belgrade Synagogue was declared a national heritage site in 2013.

names.ja: 軍事博物館（ベオグラード）
names.it: Museo di storia militare di Belgrado

en.text: The Military Museum is a museum located in Belgrade, Serbia. Founded in 1878, the museum has over 3,000 ancient and modern items.
Branko's Bridge is the second-largest bridge of Belgrade, Serbia, connecting the city center with New Belgrade across the Sava river.
The Gazela Bridge is the most important bridge over the Sava river in Belgrade, the capital of Serbia.
Terazije is the central town square and the surrounding neighborhood of Belgrade, Serbia. It is located in the municipality of Stari Grad.

names.ja: ベオグラード民族学博物館

en.text: The Ethnographic Museum is a museum located in Belgrade, the capital of Serbia. It is one of the oldest museums in the Balkans.

Tašmajdan Park, colloquially Tašmajdan or simply just Taš, is a public park and the surrounding urban neighborhood of Belgrade, the capital of Serbia. It is located in Belgrade's municipality of Palilula.

Pančevo Bridge or colloquially Pančevac is a bridge over the Danube in Belgrade, the capital of Serbia. It was named after the northern city of Pančevo which is connected to Belgrade by the road continuing from the bridge.
Beo zoo vrt, also known as Vrt dobre nade, is a publicly owned zoo in Belgrade, Serbia. Established on 12 July 1936, it situated in the historic Kalemegdan Park.
The Beli Dvor is one of two residences of the Dedinje Royal Compound in the Dedinje neighborhood of Belgrade. It was the official residence of the Prince Regent Paul from 1934 to 1941.
Topčider is a forest park and an urban neighborhood of Belgrade, the capital of Serbia. It is divided between the municipalities of Čukarica, Rakovica and Savski Venac.
The Kraljevski Dvor is the main building in the Dedinje Royal Compound and was the official residence of the Karađorđević royal family from 1934 to 1941.

names.fr: Konak de la princesse Ljubica à Belgrade

en.text: The Residence of Princess Ljubica is a palace located in Belgrade, Serbia.
Art museum in Belgrade, Serbia
Ružica Church is a Serbian Orthodox church located in the Belgrade Fortress, in Belgrade, the capital of Serbia. The original church was built in the early 15th century.

names.en: Church of Saint Alexander of Neva
names.zh-CN: 亞歷山大·涅夫斯基主教座堂

en.text: The Church of St. Alexander Nevsky is a Serbian Orthodox church in Belgrade, Serbia.

The Jevremovac Botanical Garden is the botanical garden of the University of Belgrade and also a surrounding urban neighborhood of Belgrade, Serbia. The garden is located in the municipality of Stari Grad and is administered by the University of Belgrade's School of Biology.

names.pt: Trem Azul de Josip Broz Tito

en.text: Tito's Blue Train is the popular name of the former state luxury train of Yugoslav Marshal Josip Broz Tito, president of the former Yugoslavia. More than 60 statesmen and world leaders traveled on the blue train during its service.
The Museum of Vuk and Dositej is one of the most important memorial museums in Belgrade, the capital of Serbia.

names.ja: 新鉄道橋 (ベオグラード)

en.text: New Railway Bridge is a cable-stayed bridge over the Sava river in Belgrade, the capital of Serbia.
The Pupin Bridge is a road bridge over the Danube River in Belgrade, Serbia. The bridge is located upstream of the city center and connects Belgrade neighbourhoods of Zemun and Borča.

names.ja: ニコラ・パシッチ広場

en.text: The Nikola Pašić Square is one of the central town squares and an urban neighborhoods of Belgrade, the capital of Serbia. The square is named after Nikola Pašić who served as mayor of Belgrade, prime minister of Serbia and prime minister of Yugoslavia.

names.fr: Konak du prince Miloš à Belgrade

en.text: The Residence of Prince Miloš is a museum and a former princely residence in the Topčider neighborhood of Belgrade, Serbia.
The Co-cathedral of Christ the King is the Roman Catholic church in Belgrade, Serbia. It is under jurisdiction of the Archdiocese of Belgrade and serves as its co-cathedral church.

names.zh-CN: 博德罗格号内河重炮舰

en.text: The Yugoslav monitor Sava is a Temes-class river monitor that was built for the Austro-Hungarian Navy as SMS Bodrog. She fired the first shots of World War I just after 01:00 on 29 July 1914, when she and two other monitors shelled Serbian defences near Belgrade.

names.zh-CN: 贝尔格莱德铁路博物馆

en.text: The Railway Museum is a museum located in the Savski Venac, Belgrade, the capital of Serbia.

The Gardoš Tower, also known as Millennium Tower or Tower of John Hunyadi is a memorial tower located in Zemun, city of Belgrade, Serbia. It was built and officially opened on 20 August 1896 to celebrate a thousand years of Hungarian settlement in the Pannonian plain.

The Church of the Ascension is a Serbian Orthodox church in downtown Belgrade, the capital of Serbia. It still uses the bell under which the Hatisheriff of 1830 was announced, by which the Ottoman Empire granted autonomy to Serbia.

names.it: cattedrale della Beata Vergine Maria Assunta in Cielo
names.es: Catedral de la Santísima Virgen María

en.text: The Cathedral of the Blessed Virgin Mary, also known as the Belgrade Catholic Cathedral, is the Roman Catholic church in Belgrade, Serbia. It is under jurisdiction of the Archdiocese of Belgrade and serves as its cathedral church.

names.fr: musée de la ville de Belgrade
names.ja: ベオグラード市博物館

en.text: The Belgrade City Museum is a museum located in Belgrade, Serbia.

names.en: Church of St Basil of Ostrog

en.text: Church of Saint Basil of Ostrog is a Serbian Orthodox Church located in Bežanijska Kosa neighbourhood of New Belgrade. Its construction started in 1996 and completed in 2001, and is the first church built in New Belgrade since World War II.

names.zh-CN: 贝尔格莱德圣三一教堂

en.text: The Church of the Holy Trinity, also called the Russian Church, in Belgrade is a metochion of the Russian Orthodox church in Belgrade, Serbia.

names.fr: musée des arts appliqués de Belgrade
names.it: Museo di arti applicate di Belgrado

en.text: The Museum of Applied Art is an art museum in Belgrade, Serbia. The museum contains over 37,000 works of applied art, which reflect the development of applied art over a 2,400 year span.

names.ja: デスポト・ステファン塔

en.text: The Despot Stefan Tower or Dizdar Tower is a structure in Belgrade, Serbia, built c. 1405, a couple of years after the city became the capital of Serbian Despotate under Despot Stefan Lazarević.

The Dedinje Royal Compound is a complex of former royal residences commissioned by and built with the personal funds of King Alexander I in the Dedinje neighborhood of Belgrade, Serbia, between 1924 and 1937.

names.es: iglesia de la Natividad de la Virgen María

en.text: The Church of the Nativity of the Theotokos known also as The Church of the Theotokos is a Serbian Orthodox church located in the center of the Zemun district in Belgrade.

names.local: Црква Светих арханђела Михаила и Гаврила

en.text: The Rakovica Monastery is the monastery of the Serbian Orthodox Church, within the Archdiocese of Belgrade and Karlovci, located in the municipality of Rakovica in Belgrade, the capital of Serbia. It is dedicated to the archangels Michael and Gabriel.
The Chapel of Saint Petka in Belgrade is a chapel, erected over a sacred spring, and dedicated to Saint Petka.
Manak House is a building on the outskirts of the former Savamala, Belgrade. It is located on the corner of Kraljevića Marka and Gavrila Principa Streets in Belgrade, Serbia.

names.es: Iglesia de San Antonio de Padua (Belgrado)

en.text: The Church of St. Anthony of Padua is a Roman Catholic church in Belgrade, Serbia.
The Museum of Ivo Andrić is a museum located in Belgrade, the capital of Serbia. Founded on 10 October 1976, it is dedicated to the Nobel prize winning writer Ivo Andrić.
Hammam of Prince Miloš is the former Hammam in Belgrade, the capital of Serbia. Built in 1836-37, it was declared a cultural monument in 1948.
Pioneers Park is a park in Belgrade, the capital of Serbia. Developed from the royal garden, which itself was a successor of a much older garden, it is today one of the central city parks.

Vračar plateau is a plateau on top of the Vračar Hill in Belgrade, the capital of Serbia, with an absolute height of 134 metres above sea level. It is the purported location of the 1594 Burning of Saint Sava's relics by the Ottomans.

names.de: Park der Freundschaft in Neu Belgrad
names.ja: パーク・オブ・フレンドシップ

en.text: The Park of Friendship in New Belgrade is one of the largest parks in Belgrade.

names.ja: カラジョルジェヴ公園

en.text: Karađorđe's Park is a public park and an urban neighborhood of Belgrade, the capital of Serbia.

The Monastery of Saint Archangel Gabriel, also known as the Zemun monastery is a Serbian Orthodox monastery. Its church was built in 1786, on the site of an older church in the Donji Grad neighbourhood of Zemun.
Protected cultural monuments in Serbia

names.fr: monastère de la Présentation de la Mère-de-Dieu à Belgrade

en.text: Vavedenje Monastery is a Serbian Orthodox monastery located in Senjak, an urban settlement in the municipality of Savski Venac in Belgrade. The foundations of the temple were consecrated on August 11, 1935.

The Evangelical Church in Zemun, Serbia was built in 1926–30 at the corner of Prilaz and Tošin Bunar streets. It was designed by Jewish-Croatian architect Hugo Ehrlich to serve needs of Zemun's Evangelical community at the time mostly consisted of Germans.

names.it: Campo di concentramento di Topovske Šupe

he.text: מחנה הריכוז טוֹפּוֹבְסְקֶה שוּפֶּה, היה מחנה ריכוז אשר הוקם על ידי הגסטפו וממשלת הבובות של הגנרל מילאן נדיץ', שכן בפאתי בלגרד בירת יוגוסלביה, פעל בתקופת השואה מאוגוסט ועד דצמבר 1941 ובו נכלאו ונרצחו יהודים בעיקר גברים מקהילות בלגרד והבאנאט וכן בני רומה.

en.text: The Topovske Šupe concentration camp was a concentration camp located on the outskirts of Belgrade which was operated by Nazi Germany with the help of Milan Nedić's quisling government during World War II.
Academic Park is a park in Belgrade, the capital of Serbia. It is situated in the neighborhood of Studentski Trg, in the downtown.
Crveni Krst or colloquially just Krst, is an urban neighborhood of Belgrade, the capital of Serbia. It is located in Belgrade's municipalities of Vračar and Zvezdara.
Cvetni trg or Flower Square is an urban neighborhood of Belgrade, the capital of Serbia. It is located in the Belgrade municipality of Vračar.
Lido is a non-residential urban neighborhood of Belgrade, the capital of Serbia. It is located in Belgrade's municipality of Zemun.
